newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain-EU CPI spread may slow rate cuts-banks group.
newsitem.headline: Spain-EU CPI spread may slow rate cuts-banks group.

text.p: The Bank of Spain's interest rate policy might become more restrictive if the inflation spread versus other European Union countries does not improve, Spanish banking association chairman Jose Luis Leal said on Wednesday.

"If the inflation differential versus small (EU) countries (with low inflation rates) provides a reference for inflation convergence, monetary policy (in Spain) will be more restrictive in order to allow prices to fall," Leal told journalists.
There was a consensus that money rates should decline in the next few months, but low inflation in countries such as Finland could mean money rates here come down more slowly, he said.
Nevertheless, the general trend was towards declining rates, he added.
The Bank of Spain left its key money rate unchanged at 6.75 percent at this morning's regular repo auction.
